rule: Three rules carry the feel. (A) A timed bulletin queue: each bulletin is an ordered list of lines plus an expiry; one crier shouts one bulletin at a time, one line every few seconds after a fixed call line, on a periodic timer and on a keyword. (B) A town economy that is visible: a capture pays a fixed bonus, daily income scales with a tax percentage, and when silver runs out random hirelings are removed. (C) Flat naming pools keyed by a type string, plus signs placed from a data file with a label id, and region nesting where a child inherits its parent priority.
keep: one line per beat on a timer, with a fixed call line before a bulletin
one crier with two triggers (timer and keyword) and the same content
rumour slots keyed by a word the player says
expiry on every bulletin so the world's news turns over
capture announced and paid, with a visible consequence when the town runs dry
flat naming pools keyed by culture or creature kind
region parent inheritance for nested zones
change: server owns one bulletin schedule, not one timer per NPC
zero-length bulletins rejected with a message
cap at 3 lines per bulletin and about 40 characters per line for 375 wide
warn one day before any hireling is removed for a broke zone
all text as text ids in zone data, never inline strings
faction map as zone ownership on one ledger
look_test: One zone scene flag with a square crier from the Pit roster. Compare three-line bulletin at 2.5 s gap, at 1.0 s gap, and all lines at once. Judge readability at 375 wide and whether the sequence reads as a story. Add one tavern rumour keyword and one sign label with the same content.
